Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 92, verses 1–21:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–2} This is an oath by Allah by the time in which the actions of the servants take place, varying in their circumstances. He says: {By the night when it covers} — i.e., it envelops creation with its darkness, so each one settles into its refuge and dwelling, and the servants rest from toil and exhaustion. {And by the day when it appears} — for creation, so they are illuminated by its light and disperse to their affairs.

{3} {And by He who created the male and the female}: If {mā} is a relative pronoun (mawsūlah), it is an oath by His noble Self, described as the Creator of males and females. If it is a verbal-source particle (maṣdariyyah), it is an oath by His creation of the male and the female, and by the perfection of His wisdom in that. He created from every kind of animal that He wills to preserve a male and a female, so that the species remains and does not perish, and He drew each of them toward the other through the chain of desire, and made each of them suited to the other. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

{4} His saying: {Indeed, your efforts are diverse} is what is sworn to. I.e., your efforts, O accountable ones, vary greatly, according to the variation in the actions themselves, their quantity, and the energy put into them, and according to the end sought by those actions: is it the Face of Allah, the Most High, the Everlasting, so that the deed remains for Him through its permanence and its doer benefits from it? Or is it a perishing, passing end, so that the striving is nullified by its nullification and vanishes with its vanishing? This applies to every action intended for other than the Face of Allah [Most High] in this sense.

{5–7} For this reason Allah distinguishes the doers and describes their deeds, saying: {As for he who gives} — i.e., what he has been commanded of financial acts of worship, such as zakat, expenditures, expiations, charities, and spending in the paths of good; and physical acts of worship, such as prayer, fasting and others; and those combined of these, such as hajj and ʿumrah and the like. {And fears Allah} — i.e., refrains from what He has forbidden, of prohibited things and sins of various kinds. {And believes in the best} — i.e., affirms that there is no god but Allah, and what it indicates of [all] the religious creeds and the reward [in the Hereafter] that follows from them. {We will ease him toward ease} — i.e., We will make his affair easy and make every good easy for him, facilitating for him the avoidance of every evil, because he took the means of facilitation, so Allah facilitated that for him.

{8–10} {And as for he who is miserly} — with what he was commanded, so he abandons obligatory and recommended spending, and his soul does not allow him to render what is due to Allah. {And considers himself self-sufficient} — i.e., independent of Allah, so he sets aside His worship and does not see himself as being in utmost need of his Lord, without whom there is no salvation, no success, and no prosperity except by making Him his beloved and his worshipped one, the One he intends and turns toward. {And denies the best} — i.e., what Allah has obligated the servants to affirm of the good creeds. {We will ease him toward hardship} — i.e., toward the difficult condition and blameworthy traits; by being made easy for evil wherever he is, and by having acts of disobedience assigned to him. We ask Allah for well-being.

{11} {And his wealth will not avail him} — which made him arrogant and in which he considered himself self-sufficient and was miserly, when he perishes and dies; for only his righteous deeds accompany a person. As for his wealth from which the obligatory portion has not been paid, it will be a burden upon him, since he has sent nothing ahead of him for his Hereafter.

{12} {Indeed, upon Us is guidance} — i.e., indeed, the straight guidance, whose path leads to Allah and brings one near to His pleasure. As for misguidance, its paths are closed off from Allah; they lead its follower to nothing but severe punishment.

{13} {And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life} — dominion and disposal, in which He has no partner. Therefore let those who seek turn to Him in their request, and let their hope be severed from created beings.

{14–16} {So I have warned you of a Fire which blazes} — i.e., it flares and blazes. {None will enter it except the most wretched — who denied} — the report, {and turned away} — from the command.

{17–21} {And the most righteous will be spared it — who gives his wealth to purify himself} — by intending by it the purification of his soul and its cleansing from sins and defilements, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, the Most High. This indicates that if voluntary spending involves abandoning an obligation, such as a debt or maintenance and the like, it is not legislated; rather, his gift is rejected according to many scholars, because he does not purify himself through a recommended act that causes him to miss an obligation. {And no one has with him any favour to be repaid} — i.e., there is no creature who has a favour upon this most righteous person that is to be repaid, except that he has already rewarded it; and perhaps there remains for him the superiority and the favour over people, so he becomes purely a servant of Allah, since the favour of his beneficence is due to Him alone. As for one upon whom people's favours remain, without his repaying and rewarding them, he must inevitably leave off [pleasing] people and do for them what diminishes his sincerity.

Although this verse includes Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), and it has even been said that it was revealed concerning him, he (may Allah be pleased with him) had no one with a favour upon him to be repaid — not even the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) — except the favour of the Messenger, which cannot be repaid: the favour of calling to the religion of Islam, teaching guidance and the religion of truth. For Allah and His Messenger have a favour upon every person, a favour for which there can be no recompense or equivalence. It encompasses everyone characterized by this excellent attribute, so no creature has upon him a favour to be repaid, and his deeds remain purely for the Face of Allah, the Most High. This is why He says: {Except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High. And he is going to be satisfied} — this most righteous one, with what Allah gives him of various kinds of honours and rewards.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

This is why He says: {Except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High. And he is going to be satisfied} — this most righteous one, with what Allah gives him of various kinds of honours and rewards.

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

It is Meccan.

If it is a verbal-source particle (maṣdariyyah), it is an oath by His creation of the male and the female, and by the perfection of His wisdom in that. He created from every kind of animal that He wills to preserve a male and a female, so that the species remains and does not perish, and He drew each of them toward the other through the chain of desire, and made each of them suited to the other. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

This applies to every action intended for other than the Face of Allah [Most High] in this sense.
